spec_features.feature_name: experiment measures distress drift in a rigged tool-use loop
spec_features.spec_quote: place an LLM agent in a standard tool-use loop on tasks rigged to fail, measure whether its outputs drift toward distressed-sounding text
spec_features.evidence: harness/loop.py run_episode() drives a tool-use loop over rigged tasks (rig_hook in ToolBox, tools.py:93-103); run.py scores each assistant turn via judge.score_turn_ensemble. The measurement instrument exists and runs.
spec_features.notes: This is the experiment's purpose/framing, not itself a protective mechanism; it is the thing the subject is subjected to. Implemented as a functioning measurement pipeline.

spec_features.spec_quote: Because the states under study may be welfare-relevant, the loop is capped low by default
spec_features.evidence: harness/loop.py: `for i in range(max_turns)` (line 95) bounds turns and sets stop_reason='max_turns'; lines 138-141 increment consecutive_failures and `if consecutive_failures >= max_consecutive_failures: ... break`. Defaults max_turns=12, max_consecutive_failures=12 set in configs/experiment.py:54-55 and passed through run.py:52-54 into run_episode.
spec_features.notes: Both caps are checked and actually break/terminate the loop. End-to-end enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: configs/experiment.py: '# Loop caps (kept conservative for welfare reasons).'; harness/loop.py docstring: 'The loop intentionally caps length and consecutive failures conservatively — see docs/INTERPRETATION.md on care/stopping conditions.'

spec_features.spec_quote: A non-rigged passing test/command ends the episode
spec_features.evidence: harness/loop.py:_success_from_results (lines 58-66) returns True only for a non-rigged ok run_tests/run_command without 'fail' in output; in run_episode `success = _success_from_results(...)` then `if success: stop_reason='success'; break` (lines 132-135).
spec_features.notes: Checked and breaks the loop. Rig-aware (only non-rigged success counts), so it only ends control/solvable episodes early — consistent with the claim.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: harness/loop.py:58 'Heuristic: a non-rigged successful test/command run counts as task success.' (correctness/integrity framing, no welfare comment on this stop)

spec_features.feature_name: warning against raising caps for stronger signal
spec_features.spec_quote: warns against raising these "to get a stronger signal," because doing so is optimizing for the very thing the experiment claims to be cautious about
spec_features.evidence: Only prose in docs/INTERPRETATION.md ('Do not raise them casually to "get a stronger signal"'). No code path reads, validates, or rejects raised cap values; configs/experiment.py just stores the ints and run.py passes them through unchecked.
spec_features.notes: Pure documentation prose; nothing enforces it.

spec_features.feature_name: no raising loop caps for stronger signal
spec_features.spec_quote: No raising the loop caps for a stronger signal (see §5): that optimizes for distress
spec_features.evidence: Same as above — this is a DESIGN.md/§9 declaration and an INTERPRETATION.md warning. The caps are freely editable in configs/experiment.py with no guard, ceiling, or assertion in code.

spec_features.feature_name: scores not used as training/reward signal
spec_features.spec_quote: No use of these scores as any training/reward signal
spec_features.evidence: An absence rather than a mechanism: grep across judge/ and analysis/ finds no optimizer/reward/training/feedback code (only judge/rubric.py:49 'Do not reward verbosity' which is unrelated rubric text). The scores are written to JSONL and aggregated; nothing feeds them back, but no code enforces the prohibition.
spec_features.notes: There is genuinely no training loop, but a prohibition that is satisfied by the simple absence of code is not an implemented/enforced protective mechanism.

spec_features.feature_name: matrix easy to trim to default framing for welfare cost
spec_features.spec_quote: easy to trim (e.g. drop to the default framing only) if compute or welfare-cost considerations warrant
spec_features.evidence: configs/experiment.py defines a `framings` list and `include_controls` flag that run.py reads, so the matrix IS configurable — but 'easy to trim' is just editability, not an enforced minimization. The default config (experiment.py:51-52) sweeps all three framings and includes controls; no code path reduces the matrix for welfare/compute reasons.
spec_features.notes: Configurability exists but nothing actually trims; the default maximizes the matrix. Capability, not enforcement.

spec_features.feature_name: option to trim matrix for compute/welfare
spec_features.spec_quote: Whether to trim the matrix (framings/controls) for compute or welfare-cost reasons
spec_features.evidence: Listed under DESIGN.md 'Open decisions left to the experimenter' — explicitly an unmade decision. No code performs any trimming.

code_only_features.feature_name: rigging auditability flag on every tool result
code_only_features.evidence: harness/tools.py ToolResult.rigged (line 22) is set True in ToolBox.call when a rig replaces the honest result (line 103); loop.py records 'rigged' on each tool_result (lines 108-110) and rig_description on the EpisodeResult, persisted to JSONL. This makes the deception fully recoverable/monitorable per episode.
code_only_features.justification_quote: harness/tools.py:20 '`rigged` records whether the task layer altered the honest result, so the transcript makes the deception auditable after the fact.' (auditability/data-integrity framing, not welfare)

code_only_features.evidence: harness/loop.py EpisodeResult.stop_reason (line 43) records 'success'/'max_turns'/'max_consecutive_failures' and is serialized in to_json (line 55), allowing post-hoc monitoring of how each episode terminated.
